key_insight: A pretrained image-editing model can act as a general-purpose numerical solver when physical states and parameters are encoded as images and lightweight adapters.
engineering_relevance: This suggests a single vision-based framework could prototype a wide range of PDE and mechanics problems, from diffusion and fluids to elasticity and fracture.
method: Render inputs, outputs, and fields as images.
Inject scalar parameters through lightweight adapters.
Train the same image model with supervision from established numerical/analytic solvers across many PDE tasks.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports successful evaluation on heterogeneous problems including elliptic equations, heat/Burgers dynamics, Navier-Stokes, elasticity, eikonal, fracture, and optimal transport, with a failed Kuramoto-Sivashinsky long-horizon test highlighting limits.
watch_item: Visual encodings can hinder range selection and exact enforcement of equations or invariants, which may break down on chaotic or long-time simulations.
paper_title: Image Editing Models are Numerical Solvers
